signup.alt: The Create your account form with email, password and confirm password fields.
items: **Progress.** Shows which of the four steps you're on.
**Email.** Use the address you'll pay with — that's how your payment is matched to your account.
**Show passwords.** Reveals both boxes so you can check for typos.
**Confirm password.** Type it again. You'll see a green *✓ Passwords match* when both agree.
**Create account.** Stays greyed out until both passwords match and are at least 8 characters.

inbox.alt: The Check your inbox page with a Resend confirmation email button.
items: **What to do next.** Open the email from UnyBase and press *Confirm my email*.
**Resend.** Nothing arrived after a few minutes? Check spam, then send a fresh link. We also resend it once automatically after a day.
**Already confirmed?** Go straight to the login page.

login.alt: The login page showing an Email confirmed message.
items: **Confirmation.** The link in your email lands here with this green note.
**Forgot password?** Emails you a link to set a new one.
**Log in.** New accounts go straight on to choosing a plan.

plans.alt: The plan picker with a Monthly / Yearly switch, Basic and Premium plans and checkout buttons.
items: **Monthly or yearly.** Yearly saves {save}% compared with paying monthly.
**Your plan.** The one you picked on our website is already highlighted. Click the other card to switch.
**Continue to checkout.** Opens secure checkout in a new tab.
**Pick the matching option.** Monthly and yearly sit on the same checkout page — tick the one named here.
**Already paid?** Come back to this tab. It checks for your payment by itself for a few minutes; this button checks again immediately.
**Sign out.** You can leave and come back — you'll return to this page until checkout is done.

overview.alt: The Overview page with the top menu and summary cards for subscription, vault, domains, change requests and the guide.
items: **Main menu.** Overview, Domains, Team, Vault, Changes, Settings and Help, which opens this getting-started tour and the full guide.
**Light / dark.** Switches the whole app between a light and a dark look. Your choice is remembered on this device.
**Your account.** The email you're logged in with.
**Sign out.** Always sign out on shared computers.
**Subscription.** Your plan's status. *Active* means everything is paid up.
**Vault.** How many credentials you store, and how many need attention.
**Domains.** How many you track, and the next one due for renewal.
**Change requests.** Edits still open, and how many haven't been sent to your developer yet.
**Getting started.** Opens the step-by-step tour of every screen. It shows *New* when steps have been added since your last visit.

vault.alt: The Vault page: a Sharing panel, a toolbar with filter, Check all and Add integration, and a credential card marked Failed.
items: **Sharing.** Who else can see your credentials. [How sharing works](/guide#sharing)
**Attention summary.** How many credentials need a look. Problems are always sorted to the top.
**Filter by system.** Show only the credentials for one website or app.
**Check all.** Tests every credential right now. They're also tested automatically every night.
**Add integration.** Store a new credential. [Step by step](/guide#add-credential)
**Health.** The result of the last check (see the table below).
**System tag.** Which app or site it belongs to. Click it to filter by that system.
**Check · Edit · Delete.** Test this one now, change its details, or remove it.
**Last check result.** What the provider said, in plain words, and when.

vault-card.alt: A single credential card with the token revealed, a countdown, expiry, notes and the access history opened.
items: **Provider.** The service the credential is for.
**Health.** Green means the last check passed.
**Whose account.** *Client account* means it belongs to you; *Agency account* means it's your agency's. Handy if you ever change agencies.
**Reveal.** Shows the full credential. It hides itself again after 45 seconds.
**Copy.** Copies it without ever showing it on screen — the safest way to use it.
**Expiry.** Turns orange two weeks before and red one week before it expires.
**Notes.** Anything the next person needs to know, like where to renew it.
**History.** Every check, edit and reveal — who did it and when.

vault-add.alt: The Add integration form filled in for a GitHub deploy token.
items: **Name.** Something you'll recognise, like “Storefront deploy token”.
**App / tool / system.** Which site or app uses it. Reuse the same name to group things — it powers the filters and sharing.
**Provider.** Pick the service (GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, ClickUp, systeme.io…). Choose *Custom* for anything else and type its name.
**The credential.** Paste the key or token. It's encrypted as soon as you save.
**Account.** The username or email the key belongs to.
**Who owns that account?** You, or your agency.
**Expires on.** If the provider gave it an end date, add it here to get warnings.
**Notes.** Where to renew it, what uses it, who to ask.
**Add integration.** Saves it. Press *Check* on its card to test it straight away — it's also tested every night.

vault-share.alt: The Sharing panel with the share form filled in and an existing share listed.
items: **Their email.** The address they'll log in with. They get an email letting them know.
**What to share.** One project / system, a single credential, or everything.
**Which one.** Pick the system (or credential) to share.
**Access expires.** In 7, 30 or 90 days, or until you revoke it.
**Share.** Takes effect immediately.
**Current shares.** Who has access, to what, and until when. *Revoke* ends it instantly.

domains.alt: The Domains page listing two domains with renewal dates, auto-renew status and edit buttons.
items: **Add domain.** Track a new web address.
**Auto-renew.** Whether the registrar renews it by itself. *Off* means you must renew it by hand.
**Domain renewal.** Days until the domain expires. Domains due soonest are listed first.
**SSL.** When the security certificate (the padlock in the browser) expires.
**Whose account.** Registered under your account or your agency's.
**Edit · Delete.** Update the details or stop tracking it.
**Domain name.** For example *yourbusiness.com*.
**App / tool / system.** Which site it points to.
**Registrar.** Where you bought it (Namecheap, GoDaddy…) and which login it's under.
**DNS.** Who manages its settings (often Cloudflare or the registrar).
**Expiry dates.** When the domain and the SSL certificate expire — both trigger warnings.
**Auto-renew.** Tick it if the registrar renews automatically.
**Add domain.** Saves it.

changes.alt: The Change requests page with the logging box, view tabs, bulk actions and a list grouped by date.
items: **Log box.** One request per line. Paste a list straight from your notes — bullets and numbers are tidied up.
**App / type / priority.** Which site it's for, whether it's a *Fix*, *Change* or *New* feature, and how urgent.
**Add.** Adds every line as its own request. Shortcut: [[Ctrl]] + [[Enter]].
**Views.** *Backlog* is everything still open; *Changelog* is what's done, by date.
**Copy & mark sent.** Copies a numbered list to paste into an email, chat or AI tool, and marks those items as Sent.
**Status.** Move a single item along: Pending → Sent → Done (or Dropped).
**Copy · Edit · Delete.** Copy just this one, reword it, or remove it.

changes-done.alt: The Changelog view showing a done item with a resolution note.
items: **Changelog.** Everything marked done, filed by the date it was finished.
**Copy changelog.** A dated list of what changed — ready to share as release notes.
**Done.** Finished and live.
**Resolution note.** Optional: the version, what was changed, or who did it.

settings.alt: The Settings page with the Grant access form and a list of who has access.
items: **Their email.** The technical admin's UnyBase login.
**Access expires.** A set number of days, or until you revoke it.
**Grant access.** They're emailed and can see your workspace straight away.
**Who has access.** Everyone you've granted, with *Revoke* to end it instantly.

admin.alt: The Subscriptions admin: role and scope bar, status key, and a table of workspaces with status, plan, last payment, API key, events and actions.
items: **Your role and scope.** Super admins see every workspace on the platform. A technical admin sees only the workspaces clients granted them.
**Import subscribers.** Add existing customers in bulk, so they get accounts without signing up themselves.
**Status key.** Every colour the status column can show. The worst cases sort to the top.
**Status.** Worked out live from the last failed payment: grace (0–3 days), warning (4–7), escalated (8–14), cutoff recommended (15+). Nothing cuts off on its own.
**Workspace.** The account email, its plan and billing cycle, and whether systeme.io has its signup and customer tags.
**Last payment and API key.** When money last arrived, and whether the account's UnyBase key is active or revoked.
**Recent events.** The latest payment events systeme.io sent for this account.
**Actions.** *Trial* gives free access until a date, *Exempt* marks an internal account that never pays, and *Cut off* pauses the account and every client site linked to it.

admin-audit.alt: The systeme.io segments panel with its Sync tags now button and sync log, above the Recent admin actions table.
items: **systeme.io segments.** Signups get the signup tag and paying customers the customer tag. This line says whether the connection is set up.
**Sync tags now.** Re-checks every account against systeme.io and adds any missing tags. Safe to run any time.
**Sync log.** Each tagging attempt, its result, and the error if one failed.
**Recent admin actions.** Every cutoff, restore, trial, exemption and client-site change, with who did it, when and why.

admin-trial.alt: The Start a manual trial dialog with quick lengths, an end date, an internal note and an email option.
items: **Quick lengths.** One click for a 14, 30, 60 or 90 day trial.
**Trial ends on.** Or pick any date. Access ends at the end of that day (UTC).
**Note.** For you and other admins, for example why the trial was given.
**Email them.** Tells the person their trial is on and when it ends. They're reminded 3 days and 1 day before.
**Start trial.** Full dashboard access straight away. When it ends they see the plan picker; nothing is deleted.

admin-cutoff.alt: The Cut off automations dialog, explaining that linked client sites will be paused, with a reason box and a type-CUTOFF confirmation.
items: **What happens.** The account's automations pause, its API key is revoked, and every client site linked to it on Auto shows the unavailable page. The client is emailed.
**Reason.** Saved to the audit trail and included in the client's email.
**Type CUTOFF.** A deliberate extra step, so nobody is cut off by a stray click.
**Cut off.** Reversible: *Restore* on the same row brings everything back with the same key.

admin-tech.alt: The Subscriptions admin as a technical admin sees it: only the granted workspaces, with cut off and restore buttons.
items: **Technical admin.** You see only the workspaces whose owners granted you access in their Settings.
**Status.** The same payment ladder super admins see, for your clients only.
**Cut off / Restore.** Available on workspaces you're granted. Trials, exemptions, imports and client sites stay with super admins.
**Recent admin actions.** What happened on your granted workspaces, by whom and why.

sites.alt: Admin, Client sites: a table of client apps with status, owner account, an Auto / Paused / Always on switch, last check-in and key actions.
items: **Register a site.** Add a client app and get its licence key. The key is shown once.
**At a glance.** How many sites are paused, in grace, or not checking in.
**Status.** What the app is being told right now: Running, Grace (a billing notice for the client's staff only) or Paused.
**Owner account.** The UnyBase account the site follows on Auto, with that account's payment status. *Not linked* means the switch is manual only.
**Switch.** *Auto* follows the owner's account, *Paused* shows visitors a neutral “temporarily unavailable” page, *Always on* ignores the account.
**Last check-in.** When the app last asked, and from where. Amber means it isn't calling in, so it can't be paused yet.
**Key and actions.** Edit the details, issue a new key (the old one stops at once), or retire a site that's gone.
**Builder prompt.** Paste it into Claude when building or rebuilding a client app, so the app includes the check.

sites-key.alt: The site registered dialog showing the licence key once, the next steps, and buttons to copy the key and the builder prompt.
items: **The key.** Shown once. Copy it straight into the app's hosting as `UNYBASE_LICENSE_KEY`.
**Next steps.** Set the key, add the check with the builder prompt, redeploy, then watch for the first check-in.
**Copy builder prompt.** The instructions to paste into Claude in the app's project.
**I've saved the key.** Closes the window. The key can't be shown again; issue a new one if it's lost.

sites-pause.alt: The Pause site dialog: what visitors will see, a reason box, and a type-PAUSE confirmation.
items: **What visitors see.** A neutral “temporarily unavailable” page within about a minute. Data, webhooks and scheduled jobs keep running.
**Reason.** Saved to the audit trail and included in the owner's email.
**Type PAUSE.** A deliberate extra step, like the account cutoff.
**Pause site.** Switch back to *Auto* or *Always on* and the app returns within a minute.

vault-shared.alt: The Vault as someone with shared access sees it: credentials labelled Shared by the owner's email.
items: **Shared by.** Credentials shared with you, or a client's credentials you manage, show whose workspace they belong to.
**Credential.** Reveal it when you need it. It hides again on its own, and every reveal shows in the owner's history.
**Health.** The result of the last live check, so you know a key still works before you deploy.
**Check.** Re-test the credential now. *History*, under its details, shows who changed or revealed it.
